notes:
I couldn't do this research. The tool I use to search and fetch web pages refused every request with "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." That happened on my first attempt (fetching Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Biblehub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes) and again on a single test fetch. My other tools have no internet access, so I couldn't open any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I read no pages, I have no notes to give you. I've deliberately not written commentary on Job 19 from memory, because it would have no verified sources behind it.

When the tool is available again, I'll go through these sources:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-19/
   - Biblehub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on Job 19
   - preceptaustin.org's Job 19 page
   - Studylight for anything those miss
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly vv. 25–27 (who the Redeemer is, and whether "in my flesh" means bodily resurrection or seeing God before death). I'd look at Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God, Spurgeon.org, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed, the Lutheran sites (LCMS, 1517.org) and the Pentecostal sites.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible translator notes on the hard Hebrew in vv. 20 and 25–27
   - Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship
   - New Advent and Catholic.com for Catholic readings, and OCA for Orthodox ones
   - Got Questions for popular modern teaching, if any page addresses it

Please send the request again in a new message and I'll start with those fetches.
